title: USDA FSIS: What is the Danger Zone?
text: The Danger Zone is the temperature range between 40 °F (4.4 ºC) and 140 °F (60 ºC) in which bacteria can grow rapidly. To keep food out of the Danger Zone, keep cold food cold, at or below 40 °F (4.4 ºC), and hot food hot, at or above 140 °F (60 ºC). Keep cold food in the refrigerator, in coolers, or in containers on ice. Keep hot cooked food in the oven, in heated chafing dishes, or in preheated steam tables, warming trays and/or slow cookers. Use a food thermometer to verify temperatures. Never leave food in the Danger Zone over 2 hours; 1 hour if outside temperature is above 90 °F (32.2 ºC).
